channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Uzbekistan Senate Approves Life Imprisonment for Sexual Crimes Against Children Under 14
item.description: The Senate of Uzbekistan has approved amendments to legislation, introducing life imprisonment for sexual crimes against individuals under 14. This decision follows a review of the law aimed at improving child protection systems. Statistics show a rise in reported cases of sexual offenses against minors in recent years, highlighting the need for stricter penalties and enforcement.

item.title: Foreign Tourists Spent 1.9 Times More in Kyrgyzstan Than Kyrgyz Citizens Abroad
item.description: Foreign tourists spent nearly 1.9 times more money in Kyrgyzstan than Kyrgyz citizens spent on overseas travel in the first half of 2026. Foreigners' expenditures reached $528.3 million, while Kyrgyz citizens spent $284.8 million abroad. Tourism contributed 3.6% to the country's GDP, with a significant number of businesses operating in the sector.

item.title: Russia Offers Tajikistan Expertise in Seismic-Resistant Construction and Smart City Development
item.description: Russia has proposed sharing its expertise with Tajikistan in seismic-resistant construction and smart city development. This collaboration aims to enhance urban infrastructure resilience. Both countries are also working towards launching a joint industrial park in Dushanbe soon, with a roadmap already approved and formalization steps underway.

item.title: Former Senate Speaker Maulen Ashimbayev Appointed to Overseas Position
item.description: Maulen Ashimbayev, the former Speaker of the Senate, has been appointed to a new position abroad. The details of his new role and the specific country or organization were not immediately disclosed in the report.

item.title: DABS Chief Discusses Energy Cooperation and Electricity Imports with Tajikistan's Energy Minister
item.description: Abdul Haq Hamkar, CEO of Da Afghanistan Breshna Sherkat (DABS), met Tajikistan's Energy Minister Daler Juma to discuss enhancing electricity imports and expanding power transmission infrastructure. They also explored a proposed 500kV line to Iran and energy projects in Badakhshan province.

item.title: Pakistan demands expulsion of Afghan medical students, but courts offer protection
item.description: Hundreds of Afghan students studying medicine in Pakistan face potential expulsion due to tightened immigration policies. While the Pakistani Foreign Ministry stated enrolled students with valid documents can continue, many lack official visas. Courts are issuing interim orders protecting students facing deportation.

item.title: Turkey urges stronger cooperation against disinformation in Turkic world
item.description: Turkey has called for enhanced cooperation among Turkic states to combat disinformation, hate speech, and digital manipulation. The head of Turkey's Communications Directorate emphasized the need for joint communication platforms and developing common approaches to new technologies like artificial intelligence.

item.title: Uzbekistan Sold No Gold in August as Exports Declined
item.description: Uzbekistan did not sell any gold in August, contributing to a threefold decrease in precious metal exports. The country's overall exports fell by 3.4% in the first eight months of the year, largely due to the significant drop in gold sales. This trend impacts the nation's total export performance.

item.title: East Kazakhstan Enterprise Fined Over 100 Million Tenge for Environmental Violations
item.description: An enterprise in East Kazakhstan has been fined over 100 million tenge for environmental violations. The Department of Ecology conducted an unscheduled inspection of TOO "Vostoktsvetmet" and found it failed to address consequences of subsoil use at the "Yubileyno-Snegiikhinskoye" deposit. The company was fined and ordered to rectify the situation.

item.title: First Liver Transplant Performed on Two-Year-Old Child in Tajikistan
item.description: Tajikistan has successfully performed its first liver segment transplant on a two-year-old child weighing 7 kg with congenital biliary atresia. The complex surgery took place at the National Scientific Center for Organ and Human Tissue Transplantation. Doctors noted the challenges of transplanting organs into children under 8 kg due to the small diameter of blood vessels.

item.title: 25 Homes Provided to Environmental Migrant Families in Panjakent, Tajikistan
item.description: A new neighborhood has been built in Panjakent, Tajikistan, providing homes for 25 families displaced by environmental migration. These families were relocated from hazardous areas to a suitable living environment. The project, funded by authorities and development partners from the UAE, includes housing, a medical center, and a primary school.

item.title: Kazakhstan launches seasonal flu vaccination campaign with Russian-made vaccine
item.description: Kazakhstan has begun its seasonal flu vaccination campaign, acquiring 2.1 million doses of the Russian-made Grippol vaccine. The first 564,000 doses have been delivered to regions including Almaty and Turkestan. Vaccination is free for vulnerable groups, such as healthcare workers and children.

item.title: Director of 'Semey Ormany' forest reserve branch detained in Abai region
item.description: The director of a branch of the 'Semey Ormany' forest nature reserve and his accomplices have been detained in the Abai region. A special operation was conducted on suspicion of forest theft, following last year's severe wildfires in the area.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan enhances crypto market controls, focusing on beneficial owners and AML
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is strengthening its oversight of companies involved with virtual assets. New regulations will focus on identifying beneficial owners, scrutinizing transfers, and ensuring compliance with anti-money laundering requirements to tighten control over the cryptocurrency market.

item.title: Kazakh Poet Bilysbek Abdyrazak Detained in China, Family Seeks President's Help
item.description: The family of Kazakh poet Bilysbek Abdyrazak, detained in China since December 2025, has lost contact with him. His mother, a Kazakh citizen, is appealing to President Tokayev for assistance, as the poet's whereabouts and charges remain unknown. Relatives last heard he was awaiting trial in Urumqi.

item.title: Group Illegally Extracted and Sold Manganese Ore Worth 950 Million Tenge Abroad
item.description: A group of individuals in the Ulytau region illegally extracted over 4,000 cubic meters of manganese ore from the "Vostochny" quarry in Karazhal. Using heavy machinery, they processed and exported the ore abroad, with the total value exceeding 950 million tenge. An investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Aims to Increase Employment Rate to 60 Percent by 2030
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to raise its national employment rate to 60 percent by the year 2030. This goal is part of a broader program focused on poverty reduction and employment promotion, which has been released for public discussion.

item.title: National Security Committee Alleges "Semey Ormany" Employees Facilitated Illegal Logging
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) claims employees of the "Semey Ormany" state forest reserve enabled illegal logging and timber sales. Suspects allegedly accepted bribes for access to valuable forest areas. Investigations are underway for bribery charges, with potential sentences up to 12 years.

item.title: Media Reports Suggest Israel May Have Planned Flydubai Incident as Provocation Against Iran
item.description: Iranian television channel Press TV, citing an unnamed regional source, reported that the Flydubai plane incident might have been a provocation aimed at implicating Iran and drawing the US into conflict. The alleged plan was reportedly discussed during Israeli PM Netanyahu's visit to the UAE, potentially to bolster his political standing before upcoming elections.

item.title: Conscription in Kazakhstan Continues to Concern Young Men Amidst Reports of Forced Recruitment
item.description: Autumn in Kazakhstan brings the return of conscription, with 23,000 men aged 18-25 expected to be drafted by year-end. Despite its societal importance, many young men seek to evade service due to persistent distrust fueled by reports of forced recruitment and violence within barracks, a legacy of the Soviet era.

item.title: Tajikistan, IFAD, and UN-Water Discuss Cooperation on Water Resources and Sustainable Development
item.description: Tajikistan's First Deputy Foreign Minister met with the presidents of IFAD and UN-Water in Rome. They discussed cooperation on water resources and sustainable development, and preparations for the 2028 UN Water Conference in Dushanbe. Both sides affirmed their commitment to constructive collaboration.

item.title: Kazakhstan: Employees of "Semey Ormany" suspected of organizing illegal logging scheme
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee, in cooperation with the Prosecutor General's Office, has uncovered a suspected corruption scheme within the "Semey Ormany" state forest reserve. Officials are suspected of orchestrating a large-scale illegal logging operation and selling the timber. Evidence, including financial documents and records, has been seized.

item.title: Director of Batken power company detained on extortion charges
item.description: The director of the Batken Electric Networks enterprise has been detained on suspicion of extorting $3,000. The specific details of the alleged extortion and the circumstances surrounding the detention were not immediately available.

item.title: Kazakhstan launches seasonal flu vaccination campaign with free vaccines available
item.description: Kazakhstan has commenced its seasonal flu vaccination campaign, having procured 2.1 million doses of the "Grippol" vaccine. The first 564,000 doses have been distributed to regions, prioritizing vulnerable groups including healthcare workers and children. Vaccination is underway in several regions, with full distribution expected by October 5.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Oman Agree to Prepare Preferential Trade and Investment Protection Agreements
item.description: Uzbekistan and Oman have reached agreements to prepare preferential trade and investment protection treaties. This was discussed during Uzbek Minister of Investment, Industry, and Trade Laziz Kudratov's visit to Muscat. Discussions covered trade, investment, industrial cooperation, and transport-logistics corridors. Both sides aim to simplify mutual trade by reducing or eliminating duties on certain goods.

item.title: Ukrainian Citizen Detained in Astana at Russia's Request
item.description: A Ukrainian citizen, Lyubov Rozhanskaya, was detained in Astana at the request of Russia via the CSTO. She was apprehended at Astana airport upon arrival from Istanbul. Her lawyer stated she is in a pre-trial detention center and faces potential deportation to Russia, where a criminal case for child abduction was opened in 2023.

item.title: South Korea Threatens Ukraine with Measures Over Disclosure of DPRK Captives Transfer Data
item.description: South Korean President Lee Jae-myung threatened Ukraine with "further measures" if Kyiv does not acknowledge a confidentiality agreement regarding the transfer of two North Korean soldiers and issue a public apology. The dispute arose after Ukrainian President Zelensky announced the transfer of the soldiers, who were captured fighting for Russia in the Kursk Oblast.

item.title: Central Asia to Focus on Cybersecurity at CSS 2026 Event
item.description: The CSS 2026 event will place a significant emphasis on cybersecurity within Central Asia. Further details are available via the provided link.

item.title: Frequent Power and Gas Outages Reported in Balkanabat, Turkmenistan
item.description: Residents of Balkanabat, Turkmenistan, report near-daily two-hour electricity and gas outages in several neighborhoods. Local services have not provided explanations for the disruptions, which affect daily life. Previous reports indicated similar issues in the Balkan region.

item.title: US Imposes Sanctions on A7 Payment Network Linked to Russia and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: The United States has expanded sanctions against the A7 payment network, reportedly used by Iran to circumvent restrictions and linked to Russian authorities and operations via Kyrgyzstan. The Treasury Department designated A7 a 'significant transnational criminal organization,' prohibiting transactions with its sub-agents.

item.title: Eurasian Intergovernmental Council Meeting Begins in Minsk
item.description: A meeting of the Eurasian Intergovernmental Council has commenced in Minsk with the participation of heads of government from Eurasian Economic Union member states. Kazakhstan is represented by Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov. Discussions focus on current issues of Eurasian economic integration and further cooperation within the EAEU.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Introduce Dual Education System in Universities from 2027/2028 Academic Year
item.description: Uzbekistan will implement a dual education system in universities starting from the 2027/2028 academic year. This system will train personnel based on orders from employers, with a commitment to hire graduates. The program is established by a presidential decree aimed at improving dual education.

item.title: Tajikistan to Introduce Licensing for Electricity Sales via Charging Stations
item.description: Entrepreneurs selling electricity through charging stations for electric transport in Tajikistan will require a special license. The Ministry of Energy and Water Resources announced this, defining the activity as a specific type requiring government approval. This applies to both existing and future operators. Registration and document submission on the ministry's website are necessary.

item.title: Russian Prosecutor General's Office Sues Billionaire Turlóv and His Companies in Kazakhstan
item.description: Russia's Prosecutor General's Office has filed a lawsuit against Timur Turlóv, founder of Freedom Holding and a Kazakhstan citizen, and his companies. The claim was submitted to Moscow's Tverskoy District Court. Freedom Holding stated it is investigating the claim's substance and validity, asserting no risk to its operations as it has no assets in Russia.

item.title: Tajikistan and Afghanistan's 'Breshna' company discuss CASA-1000 project implementation
item.description: Tajikistan's Energy Minister Daler Juma met with Abdulhaq Hamkor, the executive director of Afghanistan's 'Breshna' company, which is currently led by the Taliban group. They discussed the implementation of the CASA-1000 project.

item.title: Woman Recants Rape Allegations Against Police, Cites Misinformation
item.description: A 28-year-old Russian citizen, Elmira Ongarbaeva, who previously alleged she was raped by two men posing as police officers in Konaev, has issued a new statement. She stated she was mistaken and that one of the accused had no connection to the police. Ongarbaeva apologized to the police for her earlier statements, citing a lack of complete information and distress.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Review List of Exchanges for Islamic Financing
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering removing Bursa Malaysia from the list of international commodity exchanges for Islamic financing. The proposed change, detailed in a government decree draft, stems from the Malaysian exchange's alleged non-compliance with new banking law criteria. This law requires commodity exchanges to operate in countries with a sovereign rating of at least 'A'.

item.title: Oil Prices Rise Again While Other Markets Remain Cautious
item.description: Oil prices have experienced another increase, indicating a renewed upward trend in the energy market. Meanwhile, other commodity and financial markets are adopting a wait-and-see approach, suggesting uncertainty or a period of consolidation before further significant price movements.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Launches First National Satellite into Orbit
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov attended the launch ceremony of Kyrgyzstan's first national satellite from Vandenberg Space Force Base in California. The satellite, a result of collaboration with the UAE, was deployed via a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket and will be controlled from Bishkek. This launch opens new opportunities for utilizing space data in various sectors.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Denmark to Begin Negotiations on Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement
item.description: Kazakhstan and Denmark intend to start negotiations on an agreement to avoid double taxation. Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen announced this after talks with Kazakh Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi in Astana. Both ministers expressed readiness to intensify negotiations, believing it will benefit investment and economic cooperation between the two countries.
